planting.note: Pruning group 2; large early-summer flowers form on old wood, so limit hard cutting back to just after the first flush. Can also be planted in fall.

directions: Raised at the Jackman nursery in England around 1862 as part of the lanuginosa group of large-flowered clematis, 'Candida' produces broad, rounded, creamy-white sepals 5 to 7 inches across around a bold cluster of chocolate-brown stamens. It flowers heavily in late spring and early summer on old wood, with a lighter scattered rebloom on new growth into late summer. It later served as a parent in some of the classic Jackman hybrid crosses, including forebears of 'Mrs George Jackman', and its pure white coloring holds best with a little shelter from the hottest afternoon sun.

planting.note: Non-climbing sub-shrub; cut stems back hard in late winter to keep the mounding habit tidy and encourage strong new growth.

directions: Native to open slopes and scrub in northern China, Clematis tubulosa is a non-climbing, sub-shrubby species closely related to and sometimes confused in cultivation with C. heracleifolia. From late summer into early fall it bears dense clusters of small, nodding, tubular flowers in soft blue to violet-blue with recurved lobes, held above coarse, deeply veined foliage on stout upright stems. Rather than climbing, it forms a rounded clump that works well massed at the front of a sunny border, and it has been used as a parent in herbaceous clematis hybrids such as the sprawling 'Mrs Robert Brydon'. Give it full sun and average, well-drained soil, and stake loosely if stems begin to flop under the weight of bloom.
